subtopic: Zone of proximal development and scaffolding

passage: Tuition notes, Friday. Written by Eshaan, maths tutor. Chinmay, ten, taught me something this month. Two weeks ago I solved a whole fraction sum for him on the board. passage: Dear Diary, Hemant bhaiya built my whole science model yesterday, the volcano with fizzing lava. Today Ma'am said it was the best in class and everyone clapped. I should have been happy. subtopic: Zone of proximal development and scaffolding

passage: When the power came back in the evenings, Sangeeta, nine, sat on the veranda with her Kannada reader. On Monday Gopika was busy with the cows and said, "Read chapter five alone." Sangeeta stared at the long words, shut the book and went to play in the lane. Tonight their Ajji sat down between them. "Gopika, read the first word only. Sangeeta, you do the rest." Sangeeta sounded out the next word slowly, then the next, getting stuck and asking. subtopic: Zone of proximal development and scaffolding
passage: Coach's note, swimming club, 3 August. Written by Madhuri. Gurpreet, fifteen, has been learning the tumble turn since May. In June I called every step: tuck, flip, plant, push. In July I only needed to say "tuck." This week I said nothing, and Gurpreet's turns were clean four times out of five. So I have stepped back on purpose and now watch from the far end. I learned the timing the hard way: in March I stopped cueing Aman after two sessions, and he swallowed water, panicked and skipped practice for a week. I also know coaches who keep shouting cues for years, and their swimmers never trust their own bodies. Gurpreet grinned after the last lap today. "You didn't say anything." "You didn't need me to."

passage: The support queue in the Hyderabad office blinked red: twelve tickets waiting. Elizabeth, in her second week, turned from her screen. "Kiran, the refund won't go through. subtopic: Zone of proximal development and scaffolding
passage: My name is Nitin, and I've been a sous-chef for two years. When Hafsa joined our kitchen last spring, my first instinct was to grab the pan from her every time the sauce split. subtopic: Identity foreclosure, moratorium and role confusion
passage: I'm Lalremsiami, and I sit next to Damini in Class 5. On Career Day, Miss asked us to draw what we'd be. Damini drew a doctor with a stethoscope before Miss had even finished speaking. qa.a: Lalremsiami notices Damini says it like her own name, as something given and certain, while admitting not knowing what Damini really thinks.

grounding: A classmate watches a girl proudly announce she will be a doctor because her family are doctors, a role handed to her that no one has questioned.

subtopic: Identity foreclosure, moratorium and role confusion
passage: Saturday. At the family dinner, Imran, eight, stood on his chair. "I'm going to be an engineer, like Abbu and Parveen Khala!" Everyone clapped. Abbu ruffled his hair, and Imran glowed all night. Tuesday. His teacher asked the class why they wanted their jobs. Imran said, "Because I'm going to be an engineer." "But why?" asked a classmate. Imran frowned. "Because... I just am." Friday. Parveen Khala was fixing her laptop at the dining table. "Do you like building things, Imran?" He thought. "I like drawing birds." She smiled. "Birds are good too." Imran looked at her, then at his drawing book, puzzled and somehow lighter.

passage: I'm Vasudha. Since I was ten, everyone knew I'd join our family's accounts firm; my grandfather's name is painted on the board over the door. When the careers counsellor handed out interest quizzes in Class 11, I didn't fill mine in. "No need," I told Parul, my desk-mate. "Commerce, then the firm." I'm starting to wonder whether that certainty was ever mine.

passage: I'm Preeti, and this year I've been three different girls. In January I was the quiet one in the science group, nodding along about exams.
